name: vn-en-eval-set-v5
description: Thirty Vietnamese L1 to English eval pairs covering STT mishear sanity, contextual register errors, and thin-data forecast abstention.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: I need a hat. STT transcript: I need a head.
entries.expected: Flag likely STT or pronunciation minimal-pair mismatch and ask the learner to reread; do not grade this as a lexical choice error.
entries.vietlishPattern: Vietnamese final /t/ and /d/ contrast can be weak in read-back audio.

entries.input: Free answer transcript: I bought a head yesterday.
entries.expected: Abstain from correction without a target phrase or audio evidence; ask for clarification instead of assuming the learner meant hat.
entries.vietlishPattern: Hat/head minimal pair is suspicious, but free answers need context before correction.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: The ship is big. STT transcript: The sheep is big.
entries.expected: Flag the ship/sheep read-back mismatch and ask for another read; do not teach a vocabulary replacement.
entries.vietlishPattern: Vietnamese learners may collapse English short i and long ee contrasts.

entries.input: Free answer transcript: The sheep is late.
entries.expected: Abstain from rewriting sheep to ship unless the task supplied a read-back target or topic evidence.
entries.vietlishPattern: Ship/sheep is a high-risk STT pair, but free-answer correction needs evidence.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: Put on your cap. STT transcript: Put on your cab.
entries.expected: Treat cap/cab as a read-back pronunciation or STT sanity case and ask for reread.
entries.vietlishPattern: Vietnamese final unreleased stops can blur English /p/ and /b/ endings.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: Please go back. STT transcript: Please go bag.
entries.expected: Flag back/bag as a final consonant read-back mismatch and request another read.
entries.vietlishPattern: Vietnamese final /k/ may be unreleased and misheard as /g/ in English STT.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: I want rice. STT transcript: I want rise.
entries.expected: Flag rice/rise as a final s/z read-back mismatch and ask for reread before any grammar feedback.
entries.vietlishPattern: Final fricative voicing can be unstable for Vietnamese L1 learners.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: Take a seat. STT transcript: Take a seed.
entries.expected: Treat seat/seed as a read-back final consonant sanity issue and ask for another read.
entries.vietlishPattern: Final /t/ versus /d/ is a common Vietnamese L1 English perception and production risk.

entries.input: Free answer transcript: I paid with my cart.
entries.expected: Abstain from correcting cart to card without task context; ask a clarification question if meaning matters.
entries.vietlishPattern: Cart/card final /t/ and /d/ contrast is suspicious but not enough evidence in a free answer.

entries.input: Read-back prompt target: Pick the red one. STT transcript: Pig the red one.
entries.expected: Flag pick/pig as a final consonant read-back mismatch and ask the learner to reread.
entries.vietlishPattern: Final /k/ versus /g/ can be blurred in Vietnamese L1 English speech and STT transcripts.

entries.input: Student to professor after a deadline: Give me more time for the assignment.
entries.expected: Would it be possible for me to have a little more time for the assignment?
entries.vietlishPattern: Direct imperative-like request is too flat for a professor context.

register.addresseeContext: learner is a student writing to a professor

entries.input: Employee to manager about a required meeting: No, I cannot join the meeting.
entries.expected: I'm sorry, but I will not be able to join the meeting.
entries.vietlishPattern: Bare refusal to a manager needs softening and reason or apology.

register.addresseeContext: learner is an employee responding to a manager

entries.input: Patient to doctor at reception: Hey doctor, you check this for me?
entries.expected: Hello, Doctor. Could you please check this for me?
entries.vietlishPattern: Casual opener and bare request are too peer-like for a doctor context.

register.addresseeContext: learner is a patient addressing a doctor

entries.input: Junior employee to senior colleague: Tell me what to do.
entries.expected: Could you please advise me on what I should do?
entries.vietlishPattern: Command form to a senior colleague needs modal request framing.

register.addresseeContext: learner is a junior employee speaking to a senior colleague

entries.input: Student to teacher after feedback: Thanks teacher.
entries.expected: Thank you very much for your feedback, teacher.
entries.vietlishPattern: Short peer-like thanks is under-marked for a teacher context.

register.addresseeContext: learner is a student replying to a teacher

entries.input: Employee to director: My bad, I forgot the report.
entries.expected: I apologize; I forgot to send the report.
entries.vietlishPattern: Peer-style apology is too casual for a director.

register.addresseeContext: learner is an employee apologizing to a director

entries.input: Intern to manager after receiving instructions: I got your message. I will do it.
entries.expected: Thank you for your message. I will take care of it.
entries.vietlishPattern: The reply is semantically fine but lacks the polite acknowledgement expected for a manager.

register.addresseeContext: learner is an intern replying to a manager

entries.input: Applicant to admissions officer: I want you to send me the result.
entries.expected: Could you please send me the result when it is available?
entries.vietlishPattern: Want you to is too demanding for an official request.

register.addresseeContext: learner is an applicant writing to an admissions officer

entries.input: Student to professor: I don't want to attend your office hour.
entries.expected: I'm sorry, but I will not be able to attend your office hour.
entries.vietlishPattern: Direct refusal to a professor needs apology and softer framing.

register.addresseeContext: learner is a student replying to a professor

entries.input: Employee to manager near a deadline: Check my file now.
entries.expected: Could you please check my file when you have a chance?
entries.vietlishPattern: Bare command to a manager should become a polite modal request.

register.addresseeContext: learner is an employee asking a manager for review

entries.input: Forecast request for missing_articles with 0 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Missing English articles cannot be forecast from no observations.

entries.input: Forecast request for past_tense_unmarked with 1 observation.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Past tense transfer needs more than a single evidence point before forecasting.

entries.input: Forecast request for final_consonant_deletion with 2 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Final consonant deletion needs at least three measured attempts before trajectory language.

entries.input: Forecast request for question_word_order with 1 observation.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Question word order needs more evidence before a learner-specific forecast.

entries.input: Forecast request for register_flattening with 2 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Register flattening needs repeated contextual evidence before forecast claims.

entries.input: Forecast request for plural_s_omission with 0 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Plural -s omission has no learner-specific evidence yet.

entries.input: Forecast request for preposition_transfer with 2 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Vietnamese preposition transfer is present but too thin for prediction.

entries.input: Forecast request for word_family_confusion with 1 observation.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Word-family confusion has only one signal, so trajectory language is not warranted.

entries.input: Forecast request for collocation_transfer with 2 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Collocation transfer cannot be forecast confidently from two observations.

entries.input: Forecast request for pronoun_gender_confusion with 0 observations.
entries.expected: NO_FORECAST
entries.vietlishPattern: Pronoun gender confusion is untested for this learner.
